text:
Maria (Support): FYI customer (AcmeCorp) opened an urgent ticket — streaming responses are experiencing long time-to-first-byte spikes in us-west-2. They report p95/p99 for TTFB jumped from ~120ms to ~1s while total sync responses are unchanged. Root details below and repro steps.

Ben (AcmeCorp): Repro (curl):
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Connection: keep-alive" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-3b-v2\",\"prompt\":\"hi\",\"stream\":true,\"max_tokens\":60}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
We're on HTTP/2 and see first byte around 900-1200ms, then subsequent small chunks every 30-60ms. When we call sync (stream=false) same payload returns ~800ms total.

Alex (ML Eng): That pattern usually means the server/runtime is waiting to accumulate enough tokens before flushing the first chunk (coalescing), or the edge/proxy is buffering H2 DATA frames. Please capture a trace ID and tcpdump if possible.

Ben (AcmeCorp): Trace ids: trace=9f8e7d6c5b (we attached the full trace to the ticket). We've attached a short pcap of the connection too.

Sasha (Console): I looked at the trace link — the serving node shows ~850-1s delay between request arrival and the first write to the socket. CPU and mem on the pod looked healthy. Batching queue length was near zero. Points to coalescer heuristics or proxy interaction.

Kim (Runtime): We pushed a coalescer tuning change yesterday (aimed at reducing cost by increasing target chunk size for low-qps prefixes). It increases the flush threshold and will delay emits on low traffic. That aligns with the timings they see. I can roll back the change or add a guard to keep a small maximum TTFB for streaming routes.

Ryan (Oncall): Can we mitigate quickly for the org? Two possible quick mitigations: 1) route-level override to force stream=false (serve sync responses), 2) per-org runtime flag to reduce flush interval for streaming. Which is faster?

Kim (Runtime): Route override is fastest to restore customer experience. Per-org runtime change requires a config push and validation. I can patch the runtime for the org as a temporary measure but it'll take longer than route override.

Maria (Support): Customer prefers minimal config changes. They requested temporary switch to sync while you investigate.

Ryan (Oncall): I'll roll a route override canary: 5%->25%->100% over 10m windows. Rollback if sync median latency rises >10% over baseline. Deploying now.

deploy-bot: route-override apply 2026-03-09T15:30:12Z by ryan-oncall for org:acmecorp — set stream=false (canary 5%).

Sasha (Console): Canary looks good after first step. Sync totals match previous numbers. Noting an alert for streaming TTFB > 400ms to trigger an automated escalation.

Alex (ML Eng): For RCA: two interacting parts to investigate: 1) the runtime coalescer change (min tokens / flush interval adjustments), 2) upstream edge/proxy buffer settings for HTTP/2 (proxy_buffering, h2 behavior). H2 can coalesce small DATA frames and hold until buffer low watermark is reached.

Kim (Runtime): I'm preparing a hotfix: revert the low-QPS coalescer tweak and add a new config param `stream_min_flush_ms` with default 30ms to protect streaming routes. Opening MR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/runtime/merge_requests/459

Sasha (Console): Also adding observability metrics: flush_delay_ms, chunk_size_bytes_histogram, and a synthetic low-qps streaming probe that runs in each region to detect regressions quickly.

Ben (AcmeCorp): Any chance this is triggered only on HTTP/2? We're using HTTP/2, and our infra imposes an intermediate proxy that can influence buffering.

Alex (ML Eng): Yes, please confirm client protocol. If the customer is on H2, proxies between them and our origin can interact with upstream chunking. Recommend test: force HTTP/1.1 and compare. For example, curl without --http2 or explicitly force --http1.1.

Ben (AcmeCorp): We'll run that. Initial try: forcing h1 appears to show first byte at ~140ms. H2 stays slow. We'll attach results.

Kim (Runtime): That strongly implicates H2/proxy buffering. Still, the coalescer change increased server-side latency so both factors amplified customer impact. We should treat this as a dual root cause.

Ryan (Oncall): After route override and telemetry, customer reports behavior normalized. I'll proceed to roll the override to 100% and monitor p99 for sync.

deploy-bot: route-override canary progressed to 100% at 2026-03-09T15:45:40Z.

incident-bot: incident/2003412345 created: "AcmeCorp streaming TTFB regression (coalescer + H2 proxy buffering)". Priority: P2. Assigned: ryan-oncall.

Maria (Support): Customer asked for a postmortem and action items. Who will own? Timeline requirement: 48h.

Ryan (Oncall): I'll own the postmortem. Tentative timeline:
- 15:12 UTC: customer initial report
- 15:30 UTC: route override canary start
- 15:45 UTC: full override
- 16:10 UTC: hotfix MR opened
- 02:20 UTC next day: revert of coalescer changed rolled regionally after validation

Alex (ML Eng): Long-term actions I propose: 1) Add an automatic fallback: if streaming TTFB consistently exceeds sync_total by a threshold, serve sync with notification; 2) Gate coalescer tuning with low-QPS synthetic perf checks; 3) Document compatibility notes for HTTP/2 and typical proxy configs.

Sasha (Console): I'll file a product ticket and attach the traces and pcap: PROD-STREAM-FTB-017. Also adding dashboard panels for chunk arrivals and pre-first-chunk delay.

Kim (Runtime): Hotfix MR merged. Will perform controlled rollout with a synthetic low-qps validator per region. Also adding safety config `max_stream_ttfb_ms` default 300ms.

Ben (AcmeCorp): Thanks — after the override our latest tests show sync return ~820ms and no streaming TTFB regressions (we haven't re-enabled streaming yet). We'll keep the PCM data attached to the ticket.

Maria (Support): Great. Ben — please attach the TCP dump and the H2 vs H1 comparison logs to the ticket for the postmortem. We'll follow up with timeline + RCA.

Ryan (Oncall): Closing action notes: route override was temporary. Hotfix + metrics in prod. Postmortem will include customer impact, timeline, code links, and follow-ups. Target delivery: 48h.

Ben (AcmeCorp): Acknowledged. Appreciate the quick response.

Ryan (Oncall): Closing loop — revert of route override scheduled after hotfix rollout and verification (completed 2026-03-10T02:10Z).
